title: Hello, world.
status: Proposed staging boards; not captured UI or final film

shots.title: The thing you want to make
shots.action: The finished picture is the opening promise. Follow its seed through a letter, then pull back until the studio is revealed.
shots.proof: The moving image must be the same project we later edit.
shots.gate: Hero composition and seed/letter camera path.

shots.title: Put the creator in control
shots.action: Reveal source, picture and time around the same frame. Selecting the title links its string to its visible bounds.
shots.copy: BEAM LISP · Motion graphics. Written in Lisp.
shots.proof: The selected word and the source highlight share an eyeline.
shots.gate: Proposed filming UI; coherent source edit and source/object selection needed.

shots.title: Change your mind; the picture follows
shots.action: Replace Hello. with Hello, world. The measured frame grows. Attached objects make room and stay connected.
shots.proof: One visible input; one visible geometric consequence; 1.3-second readable hold.
shots.gate: Hero dependent layout and accepted-layout transition; source refresh if filmed live.

shots.title: One decision has reach
shots.action: Change one material value. Three matching instances update together; their individual identity and content remain.
shots.proof: One definition visibly controls three surfaces.
shots.gate: Shared authored definition and multi-instance control/selection in this project.

shots.title: Small program, expansive picture
shots.action: Pull back from three instances into 24. The original stays findable. A map call stays small while its family expands.
shots.proof: One rule beside many related results; original recognizable by shape and scale.
shots.gate: Author family with stable keys and actual map expression.

shots.title: Give the idea a rhythm
shots.action: The family uncoils through branches, ribbon and helix. Continuous geometry and attachments carry the camera forward.
shots.proof: Same keyed objects and seed trajectory; no cut to unrelated spectacle.
shots.gate: Compose the shared project with continuous score and explicit correspondence.

shots.title: Time is under your hand
shots.action: Pause. Scrub backward. Jump away and return to the marked pose. The seed and connector crossing match exactly.
shots.proof: Two readable returns to one marked moment; no replay dependency.
shots.gate: General-project seekable preview and equal-state/frame check.

shots.title: The beauty still has structure
shots.action: Select the original. Show a real baseline and anchor. Move the component and let its connector remain attached.
shots.proof: The highlighted anchor and actual endpoint coincide.
shots.gate: Compact inspector and picking or an honest selector/numeric transform edit.

shots.title: Keep the idea; change its voice
shots.action: Track across one surface as ink, weave and metal pass over it. Pull back to the familiar structure wearing its new finish.
shots.proof: One silhouette, notch, texture space and coral line survive every material.
shots.gate: One supported project/material route; separate GPU and vector routes are not yet unified.

shots.title: This is the world you made
shots.action: Reverse the opening move through the title’s o. The final frame contains all the decisions we watched the creator make.
shots.proof: Longer title, coral stock, family, connections and chosen finish belong to this project.
shots.gate: Art-direct the actual cumulative hero, not unrelated final footage.

shots.title: Take the work with you
shots.action: Export the accepted frame/revision. Use an honest time cut through the job; the delivered movie matches the preview.
shots.proof: An actual completed artifact, not a cosmetic progress animation.
shots.gate: General-project accepted-revision export and matching canonical frames.

shots.title: Name the medium; invite the maker
shots.action: Keep the world moving quietly at right. Hold the complete brand/category/invitation lockup from 56.2 seconds to the end.
shots.copy: BEAM LISP · Motion graphics. Written in Lisp. · Make your first scene.
shots.proof: Readable product, category and next action with no narrator.
shots.gate: An actual first-scene destination before release; never invent a URL.
